Found the bug. In `new_receiver` (tokio/src/sync/broadcast.rs:663), when the channel is already closed, `send2(None)` wrote the closed sentinel at `tail.pos` and then incremented `tail.pos`. A receiver created afterwards gets `next = tail.pos`, which points *past* the sentinel slot, so `recv_ref` thinks the buffer is empty (hangs in `recv`, `Empty` in `try_recv`).

Fix: account for the closed sentinel when creating a receiver.

part.text:
Fixed. The bug: when the last `Sender` is dropped, `send2(None)` writes a closed sentinel at the tail position and then increments `tail.pos` (tokio/src/sync/broadcast.rs:640-646). A receiver created afterwards via `resubscribe`/`subscribe` got `next = tail.pos`, pointing *past* the sentinel, so `recv_ref` saw an "empty" buffer forever — `recv` hung on `Pending` and `try_recv` returned `Empty`.

The fix in `new_receiver` (tokio/src/sync/broadcast.rs:672) decrements the starting position by one when `tail.closed` is set, so the new receiver reads the sentinel slot and returns `Closed`.

Validation:
- Repro of the issue (resubscribe + drop tx): `try_recv` now yields `Closed`, `recv` returns `Closed` instead of hanging; resubscribe on an open channel still behaves as documented
- `--test sync_broadcast`: 25 passed
- loom broadcast tests (`broadcast_send`, `broadcast_two`, `broadcast_wrap`, `drop_rx`, `drop_multiple_rx_with_overflow`): all pass
- Full `--lib` suite: 120 passed; doc tests for broadcast pass; the only failure (`macros_join::join_size`) is pre-existing on the clean tree and unrelated
